# yTunes

> yTunes is a free, independent browser extension that overlays a classic desktop music-library interface (sidebar, track list, Cover Flow) on YouTube Music. It does not stream audio itself; YouTube Music remains the player. Preferences stay on the device. Not affiliated with Apple or Google.

## Product

- Homepage: https://ankush.one/ytunes/
- Source: https://github.com/ankushKun/yTunes
- Releases / manual install: https://github.com/ankushKun/yTunes/releases
- Privacy: https://ankush.one/ytunes/privacy.html
- Terms: https://ankush.one/ytunes/terms.html

## What it does

- Runs on music.youtube.com in Chrome 121+ and Firefox 121+ (and Chromium-based browsers via the Chrome Web Store build once listed)
- Shows library sources in a sidebar, songs in a sortable list, and album art in Cover Flow or grid
- Passes play, pause, skip, and seek through to YouTube Music
- Themes: Metal, Graphite, or match the system appearance
- Can be turned off to restore the original YouTube Music UI

## What it does not do

- No yTunes account; never asks for a password
- Does not unlock Premium, remove ads, or change what the account can play
- Does not work on phones, tablets, or Safari (yet)
- Does not send library or account data to the yTunes developer
- The browser extension includes no analytics SDK; the marketing site may use PostHog (see Privacy)
- Not an Apple, Google, Spotify, or SoundCloud product

## Install

1. Prefer the Chrome Web Store or Firefox Add-ons listing when available (links on the homepage).
2. Or download a release zip from GitHub and load it unpacked (Chrome-family) or as a temporary add-on (Firefox). Steps: https://ankush.one/ytunes/#install
